chapter: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
title: Learning trombone from the undertaker Elmer Burns
summary: Working for an undertaker, he learns positions from Elmer Burns's trombone and works out his friends' trombone parts note by note.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So at that time I was working for an undertaker. His name was Elmer [Burns]. I used to drive the ambulance and I used to play the organ for the funerals and things, you know, then jump out and drive the funeral car. And Elmer [Burns] had a brass trombone, he played in the Elks band. So I told Elmer, I said, "Elmer," I said, "why don't you tell me about this trombone? I'd like to know how it works and how do you play it. I'd like to know about this."
So he took me and showed me the positions on it, showed me how to put my lip on it and how to attack the notes,
you know, how you get from one note to the other. But he made the mistake of telling me it read the same as a bass clef of the piano.
So the trombone parts in those days were simple. You know, it's more like little fill-ins.

So I took all the trombone parts home that the guys had to the orchestrations and I would go in each position till I would find the note because I'd look on there and I knew how the note was supposed to sound, and I'd go to each position till I found that note. Then I'd remember where I got it.
From then on I started playing with the band, started to practicing with the band.
